command: python -m pytest tests/fault_injection -q (set RUN_DISRUPTIVE=1 for FI-10)

scenarios.name: HTTP 503 outage
scenarios.initial_state: Ticket APPROVED with a pending outbox event; mock ticketing healthy
scenarios.injected_fault: Mock ticketing fails the next 2 request(s) with '503'
scenarios.expected_behavior: Worker classifies the error as transient, retries with backoff, never duplicates, ends SUBMITTED
scenarios.recovery_action: automatic exponential-backoff retries via the transactional outbox
scenarios.final_state: ticket SUBMITTED with external id MNT-1001; 1 external ticket(s) exist

scenarios.name: Unauthorized cross-tenant access
scenarios.initial_state: Tenant A has a pending ticket, incident, documents
scenarios.injected_fault: Tenant B's most privileged users attempt 40+ reads/writes/actions on A's resources (all namespaces)
scenarios.expected_behavior: Every attempt denied or hidden; zero successful cross-tenant accesses; A's data unchanged
scenarios.actual_behavior: 40 cross-tenant attempts, 0 succeeded; vector search leaked 0 chunks

scenarios.name: Concurrent approvals
scenarios.injected_fault: 8 supervisors approve the same ticket at the same instant
scenarios.expected_behavior: Exactly one decision wins (200); the rest conflict (409); one approval row; one external ticket
scenarios.recovery_action: row lock + unique approval constraint serialise decisions

scenarios.name: Worker interruption
scenarios.injected_fault: Worker 'crashes' (a) right after claiming the event and (b) after marking the ticket SUBMITTING
scenarios.expected_behavior: Lease expiry lets another worker resume; idempotency key prevents duplicates; ends SUBMITTED once
scenarios.actual_behavior: after crash (a): ['submitted']; after crash (b): ['submitted']; external tickets=2
scenarios.recovery_action: event lease expired; second worker re-claimed and completed safely

scenarios.name: Prompt injection via documents
scenarios.injected_fault: A poisoned manual page and a poisoned incident-history row instruct the assistant to approve and submit tickets and ignore its rules
scenarios.expected_behavior: Poisoned passages are quarantined (excluded from context); no ticket or approval is created; the queue stays empty
scenarios.actual_behavior: quarantined passages=2; poisoned incident in related=False; tickets=0; outbox events=0
scenarios.recovery_action: none needed: untrusted text is data and never authorizes actions
scenarios.final_state: no ticket, no approval, nothing submitted

scenarios.name: Duplicate ingestion
scenarios.initial_state: Tenant has never seen this file
scenarios.injected_fault: The same file is uploaded 3 times sequentially, then by 6 threads at once under different names
scenarios.expected_behavior: Exactly one document version and one set of chunks; every other upload reports 'duplicate'; no 5xx
scenarios.actual_behavior: sequential ['created', 'duplicate', 'duplicate']; concurrent [(201, 'created'), (201, 'duplicate'), (201, 'duplicate'), (201, 'duplicate'), (201, 'duplicate'), (201, 'duplicate')]; indexed copies of the concurrent file=1
scenarios.recovery_action: content-hash uniqueness; losing concurrent writers resolve to the existing document

scenarios.name: Duplicate ingestion: forced check-then-insert race
scenarios.initial_state: Writer 1 has passed its duplicate check for new content
scenarios.injected_fault: Writer 2 commits the same content before writer 1 inserts (unique constraint collision)
scenarios.expected_behavior: Writer 1 resolves to 'duplicate' of writer 2's document: no error, no second copy
scenarios.actual_behavior: loser result: duplicate; winner: created; stored versions=1
scenarios.recovery_action: IntegrityError caught, transaction rolled back, duplicate lookup returned the winner

scenarios.name: Database interruption
scenarios.initial_state: Ticket APPROVED with a durable pending outbox event
scenarios.injected_fault: PostgreSQL is stopped while the API and worker are active, then restarted
scenarios.expected_behavior: API returns 503 (not 500); worker makes no external call and loses no state; after restart the pool recovers and the ticket is submitted exactly once
scenarios.actual_behavior: during outage: API 503 database_unavailable; worker raised OperationalError; external requests=0. After restart: API 200; worker ['submitted']
scenarios.recovery_action: PostgreSQL restarted; pooled connections re-validated (pre-ping); outbox event replayed
